mechanism_evidence: Trusted-minimum mutation executes in a dedicated subprocess opening its own durable minimum store.
Platform recovery authorization is asymmetric: the recovery-authority surface owns the Ed25519 private key while the minimum-authority process receives only the public verification key.

Recovery authorization binds recovery identity, current minimum epoch/digest, target root epoch/digest/root identity/public-key fingerprint, predecessor digest, transition identity, and activation registry epoch.
Minimum authority independently re-reads authenticated root history and current durable minimum state at use time before mutation.
Missing, forged, stale, substituted, and semantically rebound recovery authorization is denied before trusted-minimum advancement.
A durable recovery ledger preserves exact replay idempotency and recovery-identity rebinding denial across process restart.
Concurrent exact recovery clients converge on one durable minimum binding without duplicate authority.
Minimum-authority outage causes zero trusted-minimum mutation.
Clean separately authorized R2-to-R3 advancement remains live after the R1-to-R2 recovery cycle.
bounded_claim: On the tested same-host process-isolated SQLite prototype, trusted-minimum advancement required a separate minimum-authority process plus an exact platform-owned asymmetric recovery authorization. The mutation process held only verification material, independently revalidated root and minimum state at use time, denied the preregistered missing/forged/stale/substituted/rebound requests, preserved replay/restart/concurrency safety, failed closed on authority-process outage, and retained clean R2-to-R3 liveness.
not_proven: OS-user, privilege, or administrative trust-domain separation merely from process separation.
KMS/HSM key nonextractability or hardware-backed recovery authorization.
Protection after compromise of both recovery-authorization private key and trusted-minimum authority/store.
Physical power-loss or storage-controller durability semantics.
Atomicity across independent remote databases or external KMS/HSM systems.
Production, release, deploy, or completion authority.
Universal correctness of model or reviewer conclusions.
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 17: isolate the recovery-authorization signer itself behind a distinct platform-owned process and durable issuance ledger. The signer must derive the exact permit semantics from authoritative root history and trusted-minimum state rather than accepting caller-supplied semantic bindings. Falsify private-key exposure, semantic injection, forged issuance, stale/noncontiguous target selection, replay/rebinding, outage, restart, concurrent issuance, post-issuance state drift, and nonplatform authority claims while preserving exact replay and clean R2-to-R3 liveness.
